sections.h2: Where is Biloxi, and why does the water matter to a seller?
sections.html:
Biloxi is a Gulf Coast city in Harrison County, Mississippi, with the Mississippi Sound along its southern edge and Biloxi Bay on the northeast side. Gulfport borders it on the west, D'Iberville on the north and east, and Ocean Springs sits across the bay in Jackson County.

Water runs through the middle of the city too. The Back Bay of Biloxi crosses it from the Jackson County line toward Big Lake, and the Tchoutacabouffa River forms part of the eastern boundary. Wikipedia's city profile lists the elevation at 20 feet, which explains why flood zones come up early in almost every Biloxi sale.

The 2020 census counted 49,449 people, the fourth-largest city count in the state.

Biloxi factDetail

sections.h2: What in Biloxi's history shapes the housing stock?
sections.html:
Biloxi's housing carries layers of coastal history. The Biloxi Lighthouse was finished on site in May 1848, and by the late 1800s the city was both a summer resort and a seafood town, with the first cannery opening in 1881.

Keesler Field was built during World War II and is now Keesler Air Force Base, home to the 81st Training Wing and the 403rd Wing of the Air Force Reserve. Legal gambling in the 1990s brought the resort casinos.

Storms are the other thread. By the measure of storm surge at the Biloxi Lighthouse, the most destructive hurricanes struck in 1855, 1906, 1909, 1947, 1969 (Camille) and 2005. Katrina came ashore on August 29, 2005 with a storm surge of about 30 feet. Houses here are therefore a mix of pre-1969 survivors, post-Katrina rebuilds and newer elevated construction, and a buyer or inspector will ask which one yours is.

sections.h2: What does the Gulf climate do to a Biloxi house?
sections.html:
Biloxi has a humid subtropical climate, and the numbers show why roofs, air conditioning and moisture control dominate repair lists. NOAA normals reproduced by Wikipedia put average annual rainfall at 66.80 inches, spread over about 111 days with measurable precipitation.

Measure (1991 to 2020 normals)Biloxi
Average daily high in July89.7 F
Average daily high in August89.9 F
Average annual precipitation66.80 inches
Days with measurable precipitation110.6 per year
Record high104 F, set August 29, 2000 and tied August 26, 2023

Practical consequences for a seller:

  • Roofs take wind and wet weather every season, so age and condition of the roof are among the first things a buyer asks about.
  • Air conditioning runs for most of the year, so an old or failing system is a real negotiating point.
  • Standard homeowner's insurance does not pay for flood damage. The city's flood bulletin says a separate National Flood Insurance Program policy is needed, and Biloxi's participation in the Community Rating System earns a premium discount.

sections.h2: What do Biloxi's flood and permit rules mean for repairs before a sale?
sections.html:
Any building, altering, regrading or filling on a Biloxi lot needs a permit from the city's Building Division, and homes in a flood hazard area face stricter standards. The city's flood information bulletin states that work under $500 carries no permit fee, and that new buildings in the floodplain must be elevated one foot above the base flood elevation.

The more important rule for sellers is the 50 percent test. If additions, remodeling or repairs to an existing structure equal or exceed 50 percent of the building's market value, the whole structure must meet new-construction standards. A storm-damaged house in a mapped flood zone can therefore cost far more to repair for resale than the visible damage suggests.

  • Call the Community Development Department at (228) 435-6280 before starting repairs on a house in or near a flood zone.
  • Look up the flood map for your address at the city's office or any Biloxi library branch, since the city keeps copies of the Flood Insurance Rate Map there.
  • Ask whether the work would count toward the 50 percent threshold.
  • Confirm any contractor holds a City of Biloxi license, which the city specifically recommends after storms.

The city flood bulletin is an older document, and FEMA's updated flood elevation maps took effect in May 2009, so confirm current requirements with the city. You can read the city's flood map page for background. Biloxi also operates an environmental court, according to the City of Clinton's community development page, which handles property maintenance and code cases.

sections.h2: Who are the nearby employers and buyers?
sections.html:
Keesler Air Force Base sits inside the city limits, and eight casinos operate in Biloxi, including Beau Rivage, Golden Nugget Biloxi, Hard Rock Hotel and Casino and Harrah's Gulf Coast. The Gulf Coast also has a large Catholic school system, with 15 of its schools in Biloxi, and Mississippi State University runs a campus in the city.

A job change or new orders can set a firm moving date, and sellers in that spot often weigh a direct cash sale against a listing on timing alone.

sections.h2: How do Harrison County property taxes work for a Biloxi seller?
sections.html:
Harrison County mails real property tax bills on December 1, and payment is due by February 1 without interest. The county tax collector's page says interest begins February 2 at one-half of one percent for each month the bill is late.

ItemRule
Bills mailedDecember 1
Due without interestFebruary 1
Interest after February 10.5 percent per month, per the county tax collector
Tax sale of unpaid real propertyLast Monday of August
Last day to pay before the saleThe Friday before the sale, 5:00 p.m.
Homestead exemption filing windowJanuary 1 through April 1

Homestead exemption does not apply automatically. The Harrison County Tax Assessor describes a regular exemption, a credit of up to $300 on the first $7,500 of assessed value, and an additional exemption for owners who are 65 or older or disabled. The Mississippi Department of Revenue adds that people 65 or older and totally disabled owners who otherwise qualify are exempt on the first $75,000 of true value.

If you disagree with an assessment, the state says to request a hearing with the county Board of Supervisors, normally by the first Monday in August before the taxes are due. Read the county tax collector's page before you list so that nothing is delinquent at closing.

sections.h2: What are the legal steps to sell a house in Biloxi?
sections.html:
A Mississippi seller of most residential property must hand the buyer a written property condition disclosure statement as soon as practicable before title transfers. Section 89-1-503 of the Mississippi Code sets that timing, and it adds that if the statement arrives after an offer is made, the buyer has three days after hand delivery, or five days after mailing, to terminate the offer.

Recording comes next. The Harrison County Chancery Clerk records deeds, deeds of trust, releases and liens. The clerk's Biloxi recording office is at 730 Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Boulevard, and its fee schedule lists $26.00 for a deed in an archive county such as Harrison, including indexing for the first five pages, plus $1.00 for each additional page.

  • Gather the deed, any mortgage payoff statement and the current tax receipt.
  • Confirm that no code lien or open permit is attached to the property.
  • Use a Mississippi attorney or title company for the deed, because the state bar treats preparing a deed of conveyance for a fee as the practice of law under Miss. Code Ann. 73-3-55.

sections.h2: When does a cash offer make sense for a Biloxi house?
sections.html:
A cash offer tends to fit when the house needs more work than a lender or retail buyer will accept, or when time matters more than squeezing out the last dollar. Cash Home Buyers makes offers on Biloxi houses as they stand, so a sagging porch, an old roof or storm repairs do not have to be finished first.

Common Biloxi situations include:

  • A house that sat through a storm season and still has deferred damage.
  • An inherited home where the heirs live elsewhere and want to settle the estate.
  • A rental with a tenant or a vacancy that has become a monthly drain.
  • A move on a deadline, such as a job change or new orders.

A cash sale still involves a purchase contract, a title search and a deed recorded with the Chancery Clerk. Compare any figure against what a repaired, listed sale would net after repairs, commissions and carrying costs.

faqs.q: Do I have to fix storm damage before I sell my house in Biloxi?
faqs.a: No law requires repairs before a sale, but the city's permit and flood rules still apply to any work you do. In a flood hazard area, repairs or improvements that reach 50 percent of the building's market value trigger new-construction standards, so check with Biloxi Community Development before starting.

faqs.q: When are Harrison County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Taxes are due by February 1 each year without interest. The county tax collector says bills are mailed December 1 and interest of 0.5 percent per month begins February 2. Unpaid real property goes to the tax sale on the last Monday of August.

faqs.q: Do I need to give a buyer a disclosure statement in Mississippi?
faqs.a: Yes, for property covered by Sections 89-1-501 through 89-1-523 of the Mississippi Code. The statement is due as soon as practicable before title transfers, and a buyer who receives it after making an offer has three days after hand delivery, or five after mailing, to withdraw.

faqs.q: Where are deeds recorded for a Biloxi property?
faqs.a: They are recorded with the Harrison County Chancery Clerk. The Judicial District 2 recording office is at 730 Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Boulevard in Biloxi, and a deed costs $26.00 for the first five pages in Harrison County under the clerk's published fee schedule.

faqs.q: Does homeowner's insurance cover flooding in Biloxi?
faqs.a: No. The city's flood bulletin states that standard homeowner's policies exclude flood damage. A separate National Flood Insurance Program policy is available, and Biloxi's participation in the Community Rating System gives policyholders a premium discount.

faqs.q: Can I sell a house in Biloxi that is behind on taxes?
faqs.a: Yes, as long as the sale closes before the tax sale. Harrison County will not accept real property payments once the sale begins, and the Friday before the sale at 5:00 p.m. is the cutoff.
